key_insight: A PatternBoost-style loop of local search plus transformer-guided generation can discover new extremal geometric constructions, especially when the search space and representations are tailored to the problem.
engineering_relevance: The work offers a practical template for using learning-guided search to strengthen lower bounds and stress-test algorithmic relaxations in geometric optimization.
method: Adapted PatternBoost/Axplorer to three combinatorial geometry tasks.
Designed problem-specific candidate representations, local moves, and surrogate ranking models.
Used exact verification to filter generated candidates and measure true integrality gaps.
evidence_signal: On stabbing unit squares with axis-parallel lines, the automated search found a gap of 20/13 ≈ 1.54, and with structured expert-initialized instances it improved further to 14/9 ≈ 1.555.
watch_item: Performance depends strongly on representation quality and initial diversity; naive setups plateau quickly and may miss stronger constructions.
paper_title: Towards Learning-Guided Discovery of Extremal Geometric Constructions: A PatternBoost Study
